record.what_it_does: Web data platform: proxies, Web Unlocker, SERP API, scrapers, and cloud browsers.
record.auth_notes: API Access uses an API key sent as a Bearer token. Keys have roles (Admin, Finance, Ops, Limit, User) and optional expiry. Native Access (proxies) uses a proxy username and password. There is no OAuth, so each end user would paste in their own key. The hosted MCP takes the token as a URL query parameter.
record.access_notes: The MCP page says new accounts get 5,000 free requests a month with no credit card required. After that it is pay-as-you-go (about $1.50 per 1K results, $8 per GB for browser navigation), and requests stop unless funds are deposited. I did not open the pricing page, so the cost of other products (proxies, datasets) is unconfirmed.
record.api_breadth_notes: Endpoints I confirmed: Web Unlocker/SERP (POST api.brightdata.com/request), Scraper API async trigger (/datasets/v3/trigger) with snapshots, Browsers, Functions, Marketplace datasets. There is also zone and account management, which I did not verify. The API is mostly scraping calls rather than CRUD, and the MCP server exposes about 60+ prebuilt scrapers.
record.blocker_notes: No blocker. Each user brings their own API key, since there is no OAuth. Usage is billed to the user's account, and the free tier is 5,000 requests a month. Webhooks are delivery callbacks that you set per scraper trigger call. They are not account-level event subscriptions.

evidence.quote: API Access uses an API key, and Native Access uses a proxy username and password.
API Access is recommended for Web Unlocker API, SERP, Browsers, Scrapers, Functions, and Marketplace.

record.needs_human: Not confirmed: whether an OpenAPI spec is published, the exact paid plan and pricing terms beyond the free tier, and the webhook details. The webhook details come from search snippets, not a fully opened page. The data-delivery page URL is a search result I did not open.
